findings.issue_text: `_truncate_title` is defined as a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration but invoked as PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), a class-level lookup on a separate workflow class that will raise AttributeError when generating merged-PR comment bodies (GitHub and GitLab); fix by calling CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title or making it a module-level function

Replay breadcrumb summarizer (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py gen_request_data) compares error event timestamps in unix seconds against rrweb event timestamps in milliseconds, so the while-loop condition is always true and all 'User experienced an error' lines are flushed before the first breadcrumb, destroying the chronological interleaving the change was meant to provide

Browser report mutual-exclusion validators (browser_reporting_collector.py) use truthiness checks like self.initial_data.get("age") instead of key presence checks ("age" in self.initial_data), so valid falsy values like age: 0 or timestamp: 0 bypass the documented invariant that the other field must be absent

All-or-nothing batch validation in browser_reporting_collector.py returns 422 on the first invalid report, so one malformed report in a payload suppresses the metrics.incr count for every valid report in that batch, a data-loss path for the endpoint's sole metric

The new ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) enforces the Literal type at runtime and rejects unknown/new browser report types that the old BrowserReport dataclass accepted, and combined with batch validation causes the entire payload to be rejected with 422 rather than just leaving the unrecognized report uncounted

Detector owner field (ActorField) may lack org-membership validation on actor assignment: owner.id is written to owner_user_id/owner_team_id with no visible check that the referenced user/team belongs to the detector's project's organization, potentially enabling cross-org actor assignment, misdirected ownership/notifications, and cross-org ID existence probing (or, if ActorField does require context['organization'], its absence would cause a KeyError/500 on every owner assignment)

Markdown/content injection into GitHub/GitLab PR comments: attacker-influenceable issue.title and environment.name are interpolated raw into the MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE markdown posted by the Sentry bot, allowing breakout of the link construct (e.g., title containing '](https://evil.com)') or code span (environment name with backticks) to inject arbitrary links/content into trusted bot comments, enabling phishing

Unbounded nodestore fan-out in fetch_error_details: uncapped error_ids from the snuba aggregation are all fed into nodestore get_multi synchronously, fetching full event blobs when only title/message/timestamp are consumed, so latency and memory scale linearly with replay error count and a pathological replay can stall the request/worker

N+1 query shape in PR comment environment lookup: get_environment_info is called per-issue inside a list comprehension over the issue list, each call invoking issue.get_recommended_event() (snuba query plus nodestore fetch) and event.get_environment() (per-event DB query), adding ~5 snuba queries + 5 nodestore reads + 5 DB lookups per PR comment in the comment-posting path

Snuba query executed even when error context is disabled: query_replay_instance and process_raw_response run unconditionally before the enable_error_context=false check, so the entire snuba query and response processing are wasted work on every request when the client disables error context; the flag check should precede the query

Page-invariant work re-executed on every page request: the snuba query and error fetch happen before self.paginate(...) with GenericOffsetPaginator, so each page request re-runs the snuba query and re-fetches all error events from nodestore even though this data is identical across pages

Whole-recording in-memory transform extended rather than bounded: the endpoint downloads all segment bytes, JSON-parses every event, accumulates all log lines into a list, then json.dumps the whole thing for a single Seer POST, with memory and latency scaling with total recording size; this PR extends the materialized list with error entries (and the sort/merge) rather than bounding it

Browser reporting collector: new BrowserReportSerializer ChoiceField on 'type' rejects unknown/future report types that the W3C Reporting API spec permits user agents to add, which the old code accepted and metric'd — causing silent data loss since browsers ignore error responses

Browser reporting collector: URLField on 'url' delegates to Django's URLValidator which only accepts http/https/ftp/ftps schemes, rejecting spec-valid browser reports with URLs like about:blank, chrome-extension://, or android-app://

Browser reporting collector: IntegerField(min_value=1) on 'attempts' rejects first-delivery reports carrying attempts: 0; if any user agent emits 0 on first attempt, every report is dropped (would escalate to P1)

Browser reporting collector: new value constraints requiring 'body' to be a dict and 'user_agent'/'destination' to be non-empty strings reject reports the old key-presence-only contract accepted with a 200
Browser reporting collector: error response shape drifted from an empty 422/500 to a 422 with a JSON body ({'error', 'details'})
Browser reporting collector: batch semantics changed from per-report processing to all-or-nothing, so one invalid report now suppresses metric ingestion for the valid reports in the same batch

Registered default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changed from 'low' to 'off', which silently disables Seer autofix automation for existing projects that never explicitly wrote the option — not just newly created ones; a backfill or feature flag would be needed if the intent was new-projects-only

Exported symbol ParameterizationRegexExperiment was removed from grouping/parameterization.py's __all__, the ParameterizationExperiment union, and its option registration without visible caller updates — any remaining importer (in-repo, getsentry, external integrations) would fail at import time; worth a grep before ship

Positional zip() over nodestore get_multi() results in fetch_error_details() (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py) misattributes error details: nodestore does not guarantee result ordering or include placeholders for missing keys, so expired/out-of-order events cause wrong title/message/timestamp to be paired with the wrong error ID, silently corrupting AI replay summaries sent to Seer

60s processing deadline on check_auth_identities (check_auth.py) will kill the full-sweep path mid-run on sizable installs, since the task retains the optional auth_identity_id entry point that iterates all AuthIdentity rows and enqueues subtasks; retries restart from the beginning, re-enqueueing duplicate subtasks until attempts are exhausted, so the sweep can never complete

30s processing deadline on parameterless schedule_webhook_delivery (deliver_webhooks.py), a likely backlog-sweep/enumeration task, can kill it mid-enumeration when the pending-delivery backlog is large (e.g., after an integration-endpoint outage), causing kill/retry cycles that re-enqueue the same payloads and potentially preventing the backlog from draining

CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), creating an inverted base-class-to-workflow dependency that may raise AttributeError at runtime if PRCommentWorkflow does not inherit from CommitContextIntegration, and is fragile coupling even if it does; helpers should live next to existing workflow helpers or the call should target CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title

project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py uses positional zip(error_ids, events.values()) against nodestore get_multi results, assuming one entry per requested id in request order; if the backend omits missing/expired node keys, ids and payloads silently misalign and errors get attributed the wrong title/message/timestamp in the Seer summary — should look up by key instead

browser_reporting_collector.py now uses a strict ChoiceField enum for type, a URLField for url, and fail-fast batch validation that rejects the entire batch with 422 on the first invalid report; since the Browser Reporting API's type set is browser-controlled and grows over time, future report types or odd URLs will cause every report in the payload to be dropped instead of counted — consider accepting unknown types (tagged as other) or skipping invalid entries

browser_reporting_collector.py cross-field validation of age/timestamp is incomplete and self-contradictory: reports with neither field pass validation, the truthiness check treats age: 0 as absent, and each validator's docstring describes the opposite field, implying spec enforcement that isn't delivered

detector.py validators duplicate the owner.is_user / owner.is_team to owner_user_id / owner_team_id mapping in both update and create with subtle differences (update explicitly clears the opposite field; create relies on initial Nones) — extract a shared helper so the two paths can't drift

project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py endpoint module now directly owns Snuba queries, nodestore fetches, and Seer prompt-construction logic instead of placing them in the existing usecases layer (sentry/replays/usecases/reader.py), making the logic hard to reuse/test and inviting duplication for other replay-summary callers

PR bundles ~15 unrelated changes (devservices config, autofix default flips, AI prompt rewrites, grouping-experiment removal, GitHub/GitLab comment changes, browser-reporting endpoint rewrite, migration gutting, workflow-engine refactors, frontend component swaps) under the title 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', damaging revertability, ownership routing, and per-change risk assessment

The default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning ('low' to 'off') is duplicated in src/sentry/constants.py:724 and src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205 and had to be updated in lockstep in this PR; if one is missed in a future change, behavior differs depending on which constant a caller reads — consider deriving one from the other

Migrations 0917 and 0920 (convert_org_saved_searches_to_views) had their data-conversion bodies removed and replaced with bare `return`, deferring to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py which does not exist in this changeset — the SavedSearch→GroupSearchView backfill never runs, so fresh installs and upgrades silently lose the org-saved-searches→views conversion with no error

get_environment_info() and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() were added to CommitContextIntegration but are invoked on PRCommentWorkflow subclasses (GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow), which compose rather than inherit the integration — the calls resolve against a class without those methods and raise AttributeError at runtime, so every merged-PR comment job crashes and comments are never posted; additionally the helper itself calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(), which is only defined on CommitContextIntegration

Browser reporting collector rewrite enforces strict all-or-nothing validation: ChoiceField(BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) rejects unknown/future report types and URLField rejects scheme-less or non-canonical URLs (previously accepted), so a single invalid report in a browser's batch 422s the whole request and drops all reports in it, including valid ones, with no useful signal to the browser

Replay summarize endpoint's error-context feature depends on raw client-supplied field query params: if the caller doesn't request error_ids the key is absent and the feature silently no-ops, and if it arrives as the raw comma-joined string fetch_error_details iterates it character by character generating garbage node IDs — both paths silently return [] with zero errors logged, and fetch_error_details' broad except Exception: return [] adds further silent-failure modes with no observability

age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check in browser_reporting_collector uses truthiness (if self.initial_data.get('age')), so a report with age: 0 plus a timestamp bypasses validation; the docstring says the opposite of what the code checks, and both fields being required=False allows reports carrying neither (the old dataclass required timestamp)

New comment template places the user-derived issue title inside markdown link text without escaping — titles containing ']' or ')' (e.g. 'IndexError: a[0]') terminate the link text and produce malformed/broken PR comments; the template's trailing \n combined with the caller's '\n'.join also yields double blank lines between entries

feedback_summaries.py now uses '\n------\n'.join(feedbacks), which requires every element to be a str — non-string feedback messages (e.g. a None message from a malformed feedback event) that the old '- {msg}' formatting tolerated now raise TypeError instead of degrading
Autofix default flipped from 'low' to 'off', silently changing autofix behavior for all new projects — an unrelated change bundled under the 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System' PR title

adjudication_records.issue_text: `_truncate_title` is defined as a @staticmethod on CommitContextIntegration but invoked as PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), a class-level lookup on a separate workflow class that will raise AttributeError when generating merged-PR comment bodies (GitHub and GitLab); fix by calling CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title or making it a module-level function

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py, `_truncate_title` is added as a `@staticmethod` on `CommitContextIntegration`, but `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` (also added there) calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` instead of `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)`/`self._truncate_title(title)`. This is an inconsistent class lookup across two different classes and will raise `AttributeError` at runtime if `PRCommentWorkflow` does not define `_truncate_title`, breaking merged PR comment body generation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Replay breadcrumb summarizer (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py gen_request_data) compares error event timestamps in unix seconds against rrweb event timestamps in milliseconds, so the while-loop condition is always true and all 'User experienced an error' lines are flushed before the first breadcrumb, destroying the chronological interleaving the change was meant to provide

adjudication.rationale: In the new `gen_request_data` loop, the interleaving condition is simply `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, but the diff does not establish that rrweb segment event timestamps are in milliseconds while error event timestamps are in seconds. In fact, the updated unit test explicitly uses second-like floats for both breadcrumb timestamps (1.5, 2.0) and error timestamps (1.0, 3.0) and verifies correct interleaving, which contradicts the claim that the condition is “always true” and flushes all errors before the first breadcrumb.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser report mutual-exclusion validators (browser_reporting_collector.py) use truthiness checks like self.initial_data.get("age") instead of key presence checks ("age" in self.initial_data), so valid falsy values like age: 0 or timestamp: 0 bypass the documented invariant that the other field must be absent
matched_golden_ids: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: the mutual-exclusion validation relies on truthiness via `self.initial_data.get(...)`, so falsy-but-valid values like `0` (for `timestamp` and/or `age`) are treated as missing and can incorrectly pass validation. Both recommend using key-presence checks (`'field' in self.initial_data`) instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-or-nothing batch validation in browser_reporting_collector.py returns 422 on the first invalid report, so one malformed report in a payload suppresses the metrics.incr count for every valid report in that batch, a data-loss path for the endpoint's sole metric

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, the code validates reports in a first pass and `return`s a 422 immediately on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., 422)`). Only after *all* reports validate does it loop again to `metrics.incr(...)`. Therefore a mixed batch (some valid, one invalid) will result in no `metrics.incr` calls for the valid ones. Whether that is a “bug” depends on intended semantics (atomic payload validation vs partial acceptance), but the all-or-nothing behavior and its impact on the metric are real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) enforces the Literal type at runtime and rejects unknown/new browser report types that the old BrowserReport dataclass accepted, and combined with batch validation causes the entire payload to be rejected with 422 rather than just leaving the unrecognized report uncounted

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the endpoint from instantiating an unvalidated `BrowserReport(**report)` dataclass to validating each item with `BrowserReportSerializer`, including `type = serializers.ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES)`. This will now reject any report whose `type` is not in that hardcoded list and will return a 422 immediately for the whole request (`return Response(..., status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)`) rather than silently accepting/metric-counting unknown types as before. This is a forward-compatibility / batching-behavior concern, but the added tests (e.g. `test_rejects_invalid_report_type`) indicate it’s intentional, so it’s not a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Detector owner field (ActorField) may lack org-membership validation on actor assignment: owner.id is written to owner_user_id/owner_team_id with no visible check that the referenced user/team belongs to the detector's project's organization, potentially enabling cross-org actor assignment, misdirected ownership/notifications, and cross-org ID existence probing (or, if ActorField does require context['organization'], its absence would cause a KeyError/500 on every owner assignment)

adjudication.rationale: While `BaseDetectorTypeValidator` writes `owner.id` into `owner_user_id`/`owner_team_id` without an explicit membership check in the shown code, the diff also adds tests that assert org-membership/validity validation occurs: `test_owner_not_in_organization` and `test_invalid_owner` in `tests/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/test_organization_detector_index.py` expect a 400 when an actor is not in the current organization or has an invalid format. That strongly indicates `ActorField` (or surrounding endpoint/serializer machinery) is performing the necessary validation rather than allowing cross-org assignment or causing a KeyError/500 on owner assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Markdown/content injection into GitHub/GitLab PR comments: attacker-influenceable issue.title and environment.name are interpolated raw into the MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE markdown posted by the Sentry bot, allowing breakout of the link construct (e.g., title containing '](https://evil.com)') or code span (environment name with backticks) to inject arbitrary links/content into trusted bot comments, enabling phishing

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new Markdown template for PR comments in `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}\n"`, and it is used by both GitHub/GitLab workflows. `title` comes from `issue.title` and is inserted unescaped into the Markdown link label, so a crafted title like `foo](https://evil.com)` can break out of the link and inject arbitrary Markdown/links into the trusted bot comment. Additionally, `get_environment_info()` returns `f" in `{environment.name}`"` and `environment.name` is also unescaped, so backticks/newlines can break the code span and inject content. There is no escaping/sanitization beyond truncation, so the finding is a real security issue grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded nodestore fan-out in fetch_error_details: uncapped error_ids from the snuba aggregation are all fed into nodestore get_multi synchronously, fetching full event blobs when only title/message/timestamp are consumed, so latency and memory scale linearly with replay error count and a pathological replay can stall the request/worker

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `fetch_error_details(project_id, error_ids)` in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, which takes `error_ids` directly from the Snuba replay instance response (`response[0].get("error_ids", [])`) with no visible cap or pagination, then does `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(...) for id in error_ids]` and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` synchronously in the request path. This makes latency/memory scale with the size of `error_ids` and also pulls full nodestore event blobs even though only a few fields are used, matching the finding as a concrete performance/abuse-risk concern introduced by the change rather than a deterministic correctness failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query shape in PR comment environment lookup: get_environment_info is called per-issue inside a list comprehension over the issue list, each call invoking issue.get_recommended_event() (snuba query plus nodestore fetch) and event.get_environment() (per-event DB query), adding ~5 snuba queries + 5 nodestore reads + 5 DB lookups per PR comment in the comment-posting path

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows per-issue environment lookup added to PR comment generation: both GitHub and GitLab workflows now call `self.get_environment_info(issue)` inside a list comprehension over `issues` when building `issue_list` (e.g. `get_comment_body`). `get_environment_info` (added in `commit_context.py`) calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `recommended_event.get_environment()`. While the diff doesn’t show the internals of those methods (so exact Snuba/nodestore/DB counts can’t be proven here), the structure is clearly an N-per-issue potentially expensive fetch introduced on the comment-posting path, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Snuba query executed even when error context is disabled: query_replay_instance and process_raw_response run unconditionally before the enable_error_context=false check, so the entire snuba query and response processing are wasted work on every request when the client disables error context; the flag check should precede the query

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get` (static/app/src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py), the code always computes `filter_params`, then calls `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to derive `error_ids` before checking `enable_error_context` (see `disable_error_fetching = (request.query_params.get("enable_error_context", "true").lower() == "false")`). Even when `enable_error_context=false`, the Snuba query and response processing still run and are only later discarded by setting `error_events = []`. This is wasted work and a performance/scope concern introduced by the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Page-invariant work re-executed on every page request: the snuba query and error fetch happen before self.paginate(...) with GenericOffsetPaginator, so each page request re-runs the snuba query and re-fetches all error events from nodestore even though this data is identical across pages

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the diff adds a Snuba call (`query_replay_instance(...)` + `process_raw_response(...)`) and a nodestore fetch (`fetch_error_details(...)`) *before* calling `self.paginate(...)` with `GenericOffsetPaginator` (and `data_fn=fetch_segments_metadata`). Because pagination is driven by separate HTTP requests per page, each page request will re-run the same Snuba replay-instance query and re-fetch the same `error_ids`/error event details even though they don’t depend on the page of segments being returned. This is an efficiency/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whole-recording in-memory transform extended rather than bounded: the endpoint downloads all segment bytes, JSON-parses every event, accumulates all log lines into a list, then json.dumps the whole thing for a single Seer POST, with memory and latency scaling with total recording size; this PR extends the materialized list with error entries (and the sort/merge) rather than bounding it

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the Seer payload is still built by fully materializing all log lines in memory: `analyze_recording_segments` does `json.dumps({"logs": get_request_data(...)})`, and `get_request_data(...)` returns `list(gen_request_data(...))`. The new `gen_request_data` additionally `json.loads(...)` every segment and now merges in `error_events` (with an in-place `error_events.sort(...)` and extra `yield`s) before building that same full list. This is a real scalability/perf/architecture concern, but the diff doesn’t show a newly introduced correctness failure—this pattern existed before and is extended by adding error context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector: new BrowserReportSerializer ChoiceField on 'type' rejects unknown/future report types that the W3C Reporting API spec permits user agents to add, which the old code accepted and metric'd — causing silent data loss since browsers ignore error responses

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes runtime behavior from accepting any string `type` (previously `BrowserReport(**report)` would not enforce the `Literal[...]` at runtime) to strictly validating `type` via `BrowserReportSerializer.type = serializers.ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES)`, returning 422 on unknown values (and tests now assert rejection of an invalid type). This does mean future/unknown W3C report types would be dropped rather than metric’d, but the PR appears to intentionally enforce a known set, so it’s more a forward-compatibility/product decision than a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector: URLField on 'url' delegates to Django's URLValidator which only accepts http/https/ftp/ftps schemes, rejecting spec-valid browser reports with URLs like about:blank, chrome-extension://, or android-app://

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`, the new `BrowserReportSerializer` validates `url` with `serializers.URLField()`. DRF/Django URL validation is scheme-restricted by default (commonly only http/https/ftp/ftps), so reports with spec-valid but non-http(s) URLs (e.g., `about:blank`, `chrome-extension://...`, `android-app://...`) would be rejected with 422 where they previously would have been accepted (old code just unpacked into a dataclass). This is a behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector: IntegerField(min_value=1) on 'attempts' rejects first-delivery reports carrying attempts: 0; if any user agent emits 0 on first attempt, every report is dropped (would escalate to P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally enforces `attempts = serializers.IntegerField(min_value=1)` in `BrowserReportSerializer`, and adds a test (`test_rejects_invalid_attempts`) asserting that `attempts: 0` is invalid and returns 422. The finding’s claim that first-delivery reports may legitimately carry `attempts: 0` (and thus this is a P1 bug) is not verifiable from the diff; the implemented behavior is deliberate and covered by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector: new value constraints requiring 'body' to be a dict and 'user_agent'/'destination' to be non-empty strings reject reports the old key-presence-only contract accepted with a 200

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly tightens validation in `BrowserReportSerializer` (e.g., `body = serializers.DictField()` and `user_agent`/`destination = serializers.CharField()` which defaults to `allow_blank=False`), and the endpoint now returns 422 on validation failure. Previously it just did `BrowserReport(**report)` (dataclass/type hints only), which would have accepted non-dict `body` or empty strings as long as keys existed and then returned 200. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral/backward-compatibility change, but it appears intentional (new tests assert these rejections), so it’s not verifiably a defect on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector: error response shape drifted from an empty 422/500 to a 422 with a JSON body ({'error', 'details'})

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the browser reporting collector’s validation failure handling from returning an empty 422 (previously `HttpResponse(status=422)`) to returning a DRF `Response` with a JSON body: `{"error": "Invalid report data", "details": serializer.errors}` and status `HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` (see `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`). That is a real response-shape/API-contract change (even if intentional and tests were updated), not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector: batch semantics changed from per-report processing to all-or-nothing, so one invalid report now suppresses metric ingestion for the valid reports in the same batch

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint.post`, the new implementation first validates *all* reports (`validated_reports` loop) and immediately returns a 422 on the first invalid report, before any metrics are emitted. Only after full validation does it loop again to `metrics.incr(...)`. Previously, metrics were incremented inline per report, so earlier valid reports would have had their metrics recorded even if a later report caused an exception. This is a real, diff-grounded semantic change to all-or-nothing batch handling, but it’s not unambiguously a defect (it may be an intentional stricter validation policy).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Registered default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning changed from 'low' to 'off', which silently disables Seer autofix automation for existing projects that never explicitly wrote the option — not just newly created ones; a backfill or feature flag would be needed if the intent was new-projects-only

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the default value for the project option `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` from `"low"` to `"off"` in `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` and also updates `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` in `src/sentry/constants.py`. There is no migration/backfill to persist the prior default onto existing projects, so any existing project that never explicitly stored this option will now resolve to `"off"` at read time. Whether this is desired is product/rollout-sensitive, but the finding’s core concern (defaults change affects existing unset projects, not only new ones) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Exported symbol ParameterizationRegexExperiment was removed from grouping/parameterization.py's __all__, the ParameterizationExperiment union, and its option registration without visible caller updates — any remaining importer (in-repo, getsentry, external integrations) would fail at import time; worth a grep before ship

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` from `sentry/grouping/parameterization.py` (deleted class, removed from `__all__`, and narrows `ParameterizationExperiment` to only `ParameterizationCallableExperiment`), and also deletes the option registration `grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent` in `options/defaults.py`, with corresponding tests removed in `tests/sentry/grouping/test_parameterization.py`. However, the diff does not show whether any remaining in-repo callers/importers still reference `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` or that option key. So the concern about potential import-time failures for any remaining importer is a valid review check (grep), but it is not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Positional zip() over nodestore get_multi() results in fetch_error_details() (project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py) misattributes error details: nodestore does not guarantee result ordering or include placeholders for missing keys, so expired/out-of-order events cause wrong title/message/timestamp to be paired with the wrong error ID, silently corrupting AI replay summaries sent to Seer
matched_golden_ids: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: zipping error_ids with get_multi() results assumes ordering/positional alignment, but the backend may not preserve input order and may omit missing keys, leading to mismatched error ID to event data pairing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 60s processing deadline on check_auth_identities (check_auth.py) will kill the full-sweep path mid-run on sizable installs, since the task retains the optional auth_identity_id entry point that iterates all AuthIdentity rows and enqueues subtasks; retries restart from the beginning, re-enqueueing duplicate subtasks until attempts are exhausted, so the sweep can never complete

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `processing_deadline_duration=60` to the `check_auth_identities` task (`src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py`) while the task signature still allows `auth_identity_id: int | None = None`, implying a potential “full sweep” code path when `None` is passed. However, the diff does not show the task body, so the claims about iterating all `AuthIdentity` rows, enqueuing subtasks, and retries re-enqueueing duplicates can’t be directly verified here. What is verifiable is that a hard 60s deadline was introduced on a task that may have an unbounded/large-work path, which is a concrete risk/scope concern rather than a provable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: 30s processing deadline on parameterless schedule_webhook_delivery (deliver_webhooks.py), a likely backlog-sweep/enumeration task, can kill it mid-enumeration when the pending-delivery backlog is large (e.g., after an integration-endpoint outage), causing kill/retry cycles that re-enqueue the same payloads and potentially preventing the backlog from draining

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds `processing_deadline_duration=30` to the `schedule_webhook_delivery` task’s `TaskworkerConfig` in `src/sentry/hybridcloud/tasks/deliver_webhooks.py`. The finding is a concrete, diff-grounded operational/correctness concern: a hard 30s processing deadline could plausibly cause timeouts/retries on a task that may need to scan/enqueue many pending webhook deliveries. However, the diff snippet does not show the body/behavior of `schedule_webhook_delivery` (e.g., whether it enumerates a large backlog or is idempotent), so the specific claim about kill/retry cycles and preventing backlog drain can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), creating an inverted base-class-to-workflow dependency that may raise AttributeError at runtime if PRCommentWorkflow does not inherit from CommitContextIntegration, and is fragile coupling even if it does; helpers should live next to existing workflow helpers or the call should target CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title

adjudication.rationale: In src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py, CommitContextIntegration defines a static helper _truncate_title(), but get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title) instead. From the diff, PRCommentWorkflow is a separate workflow class (used by GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow) and there is no evidence it defines _truncate_title or inherits from CommitContextIntegration. This creates a likely runtime AttributeError and incorrect coupling; the call should target CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title or self._truncate_title.

adjudication_records.issue_text: project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py uses positional zip(error_ids, events.values()) against nodestore get_multi results, assuming one entry per requested id in request order; if the backend omits missing/expired node keys, ids and payloads silently misalign and errors get attributed the wrong title/message/timestamp in the Seer summary — should look up by key instead

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (added in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), it builds `node_ids = [...]` and calls `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then iterates `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This assumes `events.values()` aligns 1:1 and in the same order as `error_ids`/`node_ids`. If `get_multi` returns a dict in a different order (or omits missing/expired keys), `zip(...)` will pair the wrong `event_id` with another event’s data, producing incorrect titles/messages/timestamps in the generated logs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: browser_reporting_collector.py now uses a strict ChoiceField enum for type, a URLField for url, and fail-fast batch validation that rejects the entire batch with 422 on the first invalid report; since the Browser Reporting API's type set is browser-controlled and grows over time, future report types or odd URLs will cause every report in the payload to be dropped instead of counted — consider accepting unknown types (tagged as other) or skipping invalid entries

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce strict validation in `BrowserReportSerializer` (e.g., `type = ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES)` and `url = URLField()`), and the `post` method now iterates reports but returns a 422 immediately on the first invalid serializer (`return Response(..., status=HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)`), dropping the rest of the batch. This makes the endpoint less forward-compatible with new/unknown browser-controlled `type` values and stricter URL parsing than before (previously `BrowserReport(**report)` would not enforce these constraints at runtime). However, this appears intentional (tests were added asserting invalid types/URLs reject with 422), so it’s more a robustness/product-design concern than a clearly unintended defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: browser_reporting_collector.py cross-field validation of age/timestamp is incomplete and self-contradictory: reports with neither field pass validation, the truthiness check treats age: 0 as absent, and each validator's docstring describes the opposite field, implying spec enforcement that isn't delivered

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (new in `browser_reporting_collector.py`), `age` and `timestamp` are both optional (`required=False`), and the cross-field checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `.get("timestamp")`). This means (a) a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` will pass validation since neither `validate_age` nor `validate_timestamp` runs, and (b) `age: 0` or `timestamp: 0` are treated as “absent” (because 0 is falsy), so mixed-field payloads like `{age: 0, timestamp: 1}` or `{age: 1, timestamp: 0}` can slip through. The docstrings also imply enforcing presence/absence relationships beyond what’s actually validated. These behaviors are verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: detector.py validators duplicate the owner.is_user / owner.is_team to owner_user_id / owner_team_id mapping in both update and create with subtle differences (update explicitly clears the opposite field; create relies on initial Nones) — extract a shared helper so the two paths can't drift

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py`, the new owner mapping logic is duplicated in both `update()` and `create()`: both inspect `owner.is_user` / `owner.is_team` and set `owner_user_id` / `owner_team_id`. The two paths are implemented slightly differently (e.g., `update()` explicitly clears the opposite field and supports clearing when `owner` is present but null; `create()` relies on initializing local `owner_user_id/owner_team_id` to `None`). This is a maintainability/consistency risk (logic could drift) but not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py endpoint module now directly owns Snuba queries, nodestore fetches, and Seer prompt-construction logic instead of placing them in the existing usecases layer (sentry/replays/usecases/reader.py), making the logic hard to reuse/test and inviting duplication for other replay-summary callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get` now performs additional responsibilities directly in the endpoint module: it queries Snuba via `query_replay_instance(...)` and `process_raw_response(...)` to obtain `error_ids`, then fetches event payloads from nodestore in `fetch_error_details()` (`nodestore.backend.get_multi(...)`), and then interleaves those error-derived log lines with breadcrumb logs via new prompt-construction helpers (`generate_error_log_message`, `gen_request_data`, `get_request_data`) before calling `make_seer_request`. This is all implemented in `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py` rather than being placed in an existing usecases layer (the file still imports/usecases like `iter_segment_data` and `as_log_message`, but the new Snuba/nodestore/prompt composition logic is endpoint-local). That matches the finding as an architectural/reuse/testability concern, not a concrete functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PR bundles ~15 unrelated changes (devservices config, autofix default flips, AI prompt rewrites, grouping-experiment removal, GitHub/GitLab comment changes, browser-reporting endpoint rewrite, migration gutting, workflow-engine refactors, frontend component swaps) under the title 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System', damaging revertability, ownership routing, and per-change risk assessment

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly spans many unrelated areas (e.g., devservices/config.yml adding snuba-metrics + new consumer programs; flipping autofix defaults in src/sentry/constants.py and projectoptions/defaults.py; rewriting feedback AI prompt in src/sentry/feedback/usecases/feedback_summaries.py; removing ParameterizationRegexExperiment and its option + tests; changing GitHub/GitLab PR comment formatting and adding environment info in commit_context.py; rewriting the browser reporting collector to DRF serializers + new validation/tests; gutting migrations 0917/0920 to no-op; workflow engine refactors; large frontend refactors including new TableWidgetVisualization and Explore visualize model changes). This supports the finding that the PR is overly bundled and increases per-change risk/revert difficulty, which is a legitimate review concern but not a single verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The default for sentry:autofix_automation_tuning ('low' to 'off') is duplicated in src/sentry/constants.py:724 and src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py:205 and had to be updated in lockstep in this PR; if one is missed in a future change, behavior differs depending on which constant a caller reads — consider deriving one from the other

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the default autofix automation tuning value changed in two places: `src/sentry/constants.py` (`DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` from "low" to "off") and `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (registering `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` default from "low" to "off"). This is a real duplication that required lockstep edits in this PR and could drift in the future depending on which source a caller uses. It’s an architectural/maintainability concern rather than an immediately verifiable defect in this diff (both are updated consistently here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migrations 0917 and 0920 (convert_org_saved_searches_to_views) had their data-conversion bodies removed and replaced with bare `return`, deferring to 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py which does not exist in this changeset — the SavedSearch→GroupSearchView backfill never runs, so fresh installs and upgrades silently lose the org-saved-searches→views conversion with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly turns both 0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py and 0920_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_revised.py into no-ops by replacing the conversion code with a bare `return` and comments pointing to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. That 0921 migration file is not present in this PR diff, so within the scope of this changeset the referenced “correct migration” is missing, making it unclear where/when the backfill will actually occur. However, the finding’s stronger claim that conversion “never runs” and causes “silent data loss” can’t be fully verified from the diff alone because 0921 could already exist outside the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: get_environment_info() and get_merged_pr_single_issue_template() were added to CommitContextIntegration but are invoked on PRCommentWorkflow subclasses (GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow), which compose rather than inherit the integration — the calls resolve against a class without those methods and raise AttributeError at runtime, so every merged-PR comment job crashes and comments are never posted; additionally the helper itself calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(), which is only defined on CommitContextIntegration

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `get_environment_info()` and `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` are added as methods on `CommitContextIntegration` (in `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`), but the call sites were changed to invoke them on the workflow instance: `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body()` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body()` now call `self.get_environment_info(issue)` and `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` (in the GitHub/GitLab integration files). From what is shown, those methods are not added to `PRCommentWorkflow`/the workflow classes in this diff, so these calls would resolve to missing attributes on the workflow object at runtime. Additionally, `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template()` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` even though `_truncate_title` is defined right above on `CommitContextIntegration`, which is internally inconsistent and would also raise if `PRCommentWorkflow` doesn't inherit it. These are diff-grounded runtime correctness issues that would break merged-PR commenting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Browser reporting collector rewrite enforces strict all-or-nothing validation: ChoiceField(BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES) rejects unknown/future report types and URLField rejects scheme-less or non-canonical URLs (previously accepted), so a single invalid report in a browser's batch 422s the whole request and drops all reports in it, including valid ones, with no useful signal to the browser

adjudication.rationale: The rewrite adds DRF validation via `BrowserReportSerializer` with `type = ChoiceField(choices=BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES)` and `url = URLField()`, and in `post()` it returns a 422 immediately on the first invalid report (`if not serializer.is_valid(): ... return Response(..., 422)`), so a batch containing one invalid item will cause none of the reports in that request to be processed/metric-counted. That’s a real, diff-grounded compatibility/robustness concern (future/unknown report types, stricter URL requirements, and all-or-nothing batch handling). However, the claim of “no useful signal” is not accurate because the response includes `details: serializer.errors` and logs a warning with validation errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Replay summarize endpoint's error-context feature depends on raw client-supplied field query params: if the caller doesn't request error_ids the key is absent and the feature silently no-ops, and if it arrives as the raw comma-joined string fetch_error_details iterates it character by character generating garbage node IDs — both paths silently return [] with zero errors logged, and fetch_error_details' broad except Exception: return [] adds further silent-failure modes with no observability

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the new error-context path derives `error_ids` from `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then does `response[0].get("error_ids", [])`. The code does not ensure `error_ids` is requested/returned independent of the caller’s `field` query params, so the feature can trivially no-op (empty list) when `error_ids` is omitted. Additionally, `fetch_error_details(project_id, error_ids)` assumes `error_ids` is a `list[str]` but performs no type/shape validation; if `error_ids` is ever a string/other iterable, it would be treated as an iterable of characters and generate bogus node IDs. The exception path isn’t fully silent (it calls `sentry_sdk.capture_exception`), but the core dependency on caller-supplied fields causing `error_ids` absence is a correctness issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check in browser_reporting_collector uses truthiness (if self.initial_data.get('age')), so a report with age: 0 plus a timestamp bypasses validation; the docstring says the opposite of what the code checks, and both fields being required=False allows reports carrying neither (the old dataclass required timestamp)

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py), the mutual-exclusion validators use truthiness checks: `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. This means `age: 0` (valid int) is falsy and would not trigger the error, so a payload with both `age: 0` and `timestamp: ...` can bypass the intended exclusivity. Also, since both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, the serializer allows reports with neither field present, whereas the prior dataclass required `timestamp` (and the comments suggest one of the two specs’ fields should be present).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New comment template places the user-derived issue title inside markdown link text without escaping — titles containing ']' or ')' (e.g. 'IndexError: a[0]') terminate the link text and produce malformed/broken PR comments; the template's trailing \n combined with the caller's '\n'.join also yields double blank lines between entries

adjudication.rationale:
In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE = "* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}
"` interpolates `issue.title` directly into Markdown link text via `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` (called from both GitHub and GitLab integrations). There is no escaping/sanitization of `]`, `)`, etc., so titles like `IndexError: a[0]` can break the Markdown link and produce malformed PR comments. Additionally, because the template includes a trailing `
` and the caller builds `issue_list` with `"
".join(...)`, entries will be separated by two newline characters (creating a blank line between bullets), matching the finding’s spacing concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feedback_summaries.py now uses '\n------\n'.join(feedbacks), which requires every element to be a str — non-string feedback messages (e.g. a None message from a malformed feedback event) that the old '- {msg}' formatting tolerated now raise TypeError instead of degrading

adjudication.rationale:
In `src/sentry/feedback/usecases/feedback_summaries.py`, `feedbacks_string` was changed from `"
".join(f"- {msg}" for msg in feedbacks)` (which stringifies any element via the f-string, including `None`) to `"
------
".join(feedbacks)`, which will raise `TypeError` if any element is not a `str`. The diff doesn’t show the type/validation of `feedbacks`, so it’s not fully verifiable as an actual runtime bug here, but it is a concrete robustness/regression risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Autofix default flipped from 'low' to 'off', silently changing autofix behavior for all new projects — an unrelated change bundled under the 'Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System' PR title

adjudication.rationale: The diff does flip the default autofix tuning from "low" to "off" in two places: `src/sentry/constants.py` (`DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT`) and `src/sentry/projectoptions/defaults.py` (registered default for `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning`). Corresponding tests were updated to expect "off" as the default. This is a real product/behavior change (new projects will default differently) but it’s not inherently a correctness defect; the review concern is scope/intent (an unrelated default change bundled into a PR with a different title).
